name: VIX-Complex Call Spread / 1x2 Call Ratio Tail Hedge
summary: A tail hedge bought on the volatility complex rather than on the index itself - a call spread (or a financed 1x2 call ratio) that pays when volatility spikes, sized so the ongoing cost is a known annual drag.

legs.strike_rule: VXX or UVXY call, delta 0.30-0.40 (VIX options themselves are index options and are NOT available on Alpaca; the volatility ETPs are the share-settled proxy)
further OTM call, delta 0.10-0.15, financing the long; the RATIO version sells 2 of these and is a different, blocked structure

max_profit: (short strike - long strike - net debit) x 100 per unit for the spread version; the 1x2 ratio's profit peaks at the short strike and then reverses
max_loss: The net debit for the call spread version. For the 1x2 ratio version: UNLIMITED above the short strike, which on a volatility ETP that can triple in a week is a genuine ruin risk.
breakevens: long strike + net debit per share; the ratio version adds an upper breakeven above which it loses

greeks.delta: positive on a product that is itself negatively correlated to equities - this is the hedge's whole purpose
greeks.theta: negative, and compounded by the ETP's own roll decay

when_to_use: As a portfolio tail hedge when index put protection is expensive relative to volatility-complex calls - typically in calm markets with a steep VIX futures contango. It complements, and does not replace, the bank's OTM index put hedge: the put hedges price, this hedges the volatility repricing.
entry_rules: VIX index options are European, cash-settled and NOT tradeable on Alpaca. Only VXX, UVXY, VIXY and similar share-settled ETP options may be used, and their decay characteristics are materially worse than VIX futures options - document the proxy in every log line.

CALL SPREAD VERSION ONLY at level 3. The 1x2 call ratio (buy 1, sell 2) leaves one uncovered short call on a product that can double overnight - BLOCKED, level 4, and it should be rejected at the router even if approval is later raised.
Entry only when VIX spot is below 16 and the VIX futures term structure is in contango - buying vol-of-vol after the spike is how this hedge loses money.
Annual budget cap: total premium spent on volatility-complex hedges <= 1.5% of equity per year, tracked cumulatively across rolls.
Long strike delta 0.30-0.40, short strike delta 0.10-0.15, both legs same expiry, OI >= 250.
Position sized so a VIX move from 15 to 35 produces a hedge gain of 3-6% of equity - model it before entry, do not guess.
management_rules: Monetize on a spike: sell the spread when it reaches 4x the debit paid, or when VIX spot exceeds 30, whichever comes first. A tail hedge that is never monetized is just a fee.
Roll quarterly at 30 DTE, resetting strikes to the current delta targets; count each roll against the annual budget.
Do not roll strikes up during a spike to 'keep the hedge on' - take the money, then re-establish after the term structure returns to contango.
Halve the position if the ETP has undergone a reverse split within the last 30 days; strike continuity after a split is a frequent source of sizing errors.
exit_rules: Close both legs at least 2 trading days before expiry; never allow auto-exercise on a leveraged volatility ETP.
Close the short call at extrinsic < $0.10 or delta >= 0.85 - assignment creates a naked short position in a product that can gap 40% overnight.
Close the entire hedge immediately if the ETP announces a reverse split, a change in index methodology, or a suspension of creations.
Never hold a short ETP call leg through a spike on the theory that the long leg covers it - it does, for money, but assignment still delivers a short share position.
assignment_risk: One short call, covered by a long call at a lower strike, so the money loss is defined. The delivery is not benign: assignment on a leveraged volatility ETP creates a short share position in the single most gap-prone instrument available, on the exact day the hedge is meant to be working.
buying_power: Spread width x 100 minus the credit, per unit - defined.
liquidity_needs: VXX options are liquid; UVXY less so and its splits complicate strike history. Avoid the thinner VIXY chain.
common_mistakes: Assuming a VXX call is a VIX call - the ETP's roll decay means it underperforms the index badly in contango; running the 1x2 ratio for zero cost and carrying an uncovered short call on a product that can triple; never monetizing the hedge.
zero_dte_notes: Not appropriate - a tail hedge needs months of standing exposure.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
